### `bug-concordance-signature-quire-model` — hp.db page_concordance's signature/quire columns are a uniform reconstruction that omits a whole gathering

**✅ done** · bug · priority 3 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Split out 2026-09-20 from bug-concordance-section-drift, which carried it as 'related' and whose fix falsified the other half of the same hypothesis. page_concordance.signature / quire / leaf_in_quire is a reconstruction, and it is wrong early. Dumped: 29 quires -- a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r s t x y z, then A B C D E F G -- every one of eight leaves except z and G at four, totalling exactly 448 pages. Two faults, both measured against the signatures actually printed at the foot of the scans.

(1) IT OMITS THE 'u' GATHERING. Its lowercase run goes ...s t x y z, with no u between t and x.

(2) Its page-to-signature mapping is consequently wrong on both sides of the gap, in opposite directions: it places quire n two pages LATER than the scan does, and quire y fourteen pages EARLIER. hp1499_p195.jpg is signed 'n iii' -- leaf 3 recto, so quire n opens at page_seq 191, where the model says 193 (measured in bug-plate-page-seq-offset, which opened that scan for its full-page rotunda section). hp1499_p337.jpg is signed 'y ii', so quire y opens at 335, where the model says 321 (measured here, 2026-09-20). hp1499_p387.jpg is signed 'B' and p389 'B ii', so Book II's quire B opens at 387, where the model says 361 (measured in bug-concordance-section-drift).

The three readings are self-consistent with sixteen-page gatherings AND a u quire: counting u in, n to y is nine gatherings, and 191 + 9*16 = 335 exactly; and Book II's A opening at page_seq 371 (measured: our p.381, 'POLIPHILO BEGINS THE SECOND BOOK') puts B at 387, exactly where the scan signs it. The residual two pages before quire n are NOT explained by this, and want one more scan carrying a visible signature somewhere in quires a-m.

The table also stops at page_seq 448 while the book runs to at least 457 -- our p.467, the errata leaf and the Aldine colophon.

**Acceptance.** Either a measured quire table beside coverage_seed.py, keyed to signatures actually read off the scans, or a plain statement in the ledger that hp.db's signature / quire / leaf_in_quire columns are not to be used for anything. Machine-checkable: for every scan whose signature has been read, the table agrees with it -- at least the four already measured, page_seq 195 'n iii', 337 'y ii', 387 'B', 389 'B ii'. The corpus at C:\Dev\hypnerotomachia polyphili is read-only from here, so no fix may be written into hp.db.

**Risk.** Low while nothing reads those columns, and nothing in this repo does today. It matters indirectly: woodcut_catalog.page_seq was placed by subject-matching against the woodcuts table, which carries these same signature labels (see its link_basis), so every plate page inherits whatever the quire model got wrong -- which is already why plate pages travel with a +/-2 caveat. The danger is anyone deriving a page from a signature, or 'correcting' a plate page by a leaf, instead of opening the scan.

**Resolution.** A MEASURED QUIRE TABLE, built and guarded, and the ticket's unexplained residual explained. MEASURED_QUIRES and check_quires() are now in scripts/coverage_seed.py and the collation is emitted as coverage.json quires_1499 in both numberings. Twelve new signatures were read off scans this pass — p31 'c', p63 'e', p95 'g', p127 'i', p129 'i ii', p149 'k iiii', p165 'l iiii', p213 'o iiii', p275 's iii', p307 'u iii', p319 'x', p419 'D' — joining the four the ticket already had (p195 'n iii', p337 'y ii', p387 'B', p389 'B ii') and p435 'E', which bug-woodcut-catalog-page-jitter had recorded in passing. Seventeen readings in all, plus four scans (p23, p59, p87, p105) confirmed to carry NO signature. SCAN p307 IS SIGNED 'u iii', which is the direct proof the ticket asked for that the u gathering exists and hp.db is simply missing it. The model that fits all seventeen with nothing left over: four unsigned preliminary leaves, then a-y in EIGHTS (u included), z in TEN, A-E in eights, F in four = 4 + 176 + 10 + 40 + 4 = 234 leaves = 468 pages, exactly the length of the book (our pp.1-467 plus a final blank verso). THE TWO-PAGE RESIDUAL BEFORE QUIRE n IS NOW EXPLAINED, and the explanation is not a fudge: hp.db's page_seq 1 is NOT a1r. Quire a opens two pages earlier, on our p.9 — the last preliminary leaf, the one carrying Poliphilo's dedication to Polia — so page_seq 1 is a2r. That single leaf is the whole of the discrepancy the ticket measured at quire n, and it also fixes i at 127 (not 129) where the scan signs it. z's ten leaves are the one thing NOT seen directly: the corpus folder holds no scan between page_seq 349 and 363, so z is fixed by arithmetic between y at 335 (scan) and A at 371 (measured text) rather than by a signature. Recorded as such in the source. The ledger also now says in terms, under page_numbering.quires_caveat, that hp.db's signature / quire / leaf_in_quire columns are not to be used for anything, and that a page must never be derived from a signature. Nothing was written into hp.db.

**Files.** `scripts/coverage_seed.py` · `research/coverage.json`

**See.** bug-concordance-section-drift · bug-plate-page-seq-offset


### `bug-early-chapter-tags-drift-from-1499-pagination` — tours.json's chapter tags for chapters I-III put Dallington content on the wrong 1499 chapter, so no page range can be added without inventing one

**✅ done** · bug · priority 3 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Found 2026-09-20 sweeping for the same first-stop-wins shape closed in debt-reading-station-is-chapter-grained (chapter X). Chapters I (stops plain/wood/great_oak), II (wood/palm_plain) and III (horse/colossus/elephant x2) each carry multiple stops under one "half": "dallington" chapter tag, and chapter_to_station() picks the first and strands the rest exactly as it did for chapter X -- confirmed live in the regenerated reading.json: every page of manifest chapter III (pp.20-29) resolves to `valley` and every page of chapter IV (pp.30-46) to `portal`; `horse`, `colossus` and `elephant` never fire.

Unlike chapter X, this is not just a resolution gap: the chapter TAGS tours.json gives these stops disagree with translation/en/*.md, which is the text reading.json actually displays. tours.json's `palm_plain` stop (tagged chapter II, "The Palm and the Wolf") describes a palm-grove and a famished wolf; that text is on p.21, which translation/en/page_021.md and manifest.json both call chapter III. tours.json's `great_oak` stop (tagged chapter I) describes Poliphilo falling asleep under the ancient oak into the deeper dream; that text is on p.19, chapter II. Same class as the already-open bug-dallington-page-drift, which found this starting 'about chapter XIV' -- it starts by chapter I.

**Acceptance.** Each of the plain/wood/great_oak, wood/palm_plain and horse/colossus/elephant/elephant stops carries a chapter tag and a "pages" range that both match translation/en/page_NNN.md's own header for the page the stop's lede describes. A spot check of p.19 (great_oak), p.21 (palm_plain) and pp.30-46 (horse/colossus/elephant, currently chapter IV in the manifest, tagged III in tours.json) finds each cited stop's content on the page its own tag and range claim.

**Risk.** Retagging these five-plus stops without reading each one's actual page first would repeat exactly the mistake this ticket is about -- do not mass-retag by pattern-matching Dallington chapter numbers to manifest chapter numbers, because bug-dallington-page-drift already shows the two numberings are not a constant offset from each other past a certain point, and this ticket's own evidence shows that point is earlier than previously measured.

**Resolution.** DONE. Every stop was read against the page its lede actually describes, and against that page's own header in translation/en/, before it was touched. Nothing was retagged by pattern.

TWO TAGS WERE WRONG, exactly as the ticket said:
  great_oak, I to II. The oak is our p.19: beneath a rough and most ancient oak, in the midst of a spacious and grassy meadow, he lays himself down upon the dewy herbs. Headed Chapter II.
  palm_plain, II to III. The palm grove and the famished wolf on the right hand are our p.21, headed Chapter III, and plate #4 is on that leaf.

FOUR MORE WERE WRONG BY A WHOLE CHAPTER, and the ticket had under-counted them: horse, colossus and both elephant stops were tagged III, and all four are chapter IV. Chapter IV's own argument on our p.30 settles it by naming the sequence outright — a horse, a lying colossus, an elephant, and above all a most elegant gate — and the plates agree: #6 the winged horse on our p.32, #7 and #8 the pedestal ends with EQVVS INFOELICITATIS on p.33.

RANGES, read off the English page by page and not off the tour prose: plain I [11,13]; wood I [14,15]; wood II [16,18]; great_oak II [19,19]; palm_plain III [20,21]; valley II-III [22,29]; horse IV [30,34]; colossus IV [35,36]; elephant IV [37,40]; elephant IV [41,41]; portal IV [43,46].

The seams that are not obvious: the colossus appears only partway down p.35, after that page has finished with the horse and glimpsed the elephant, so [35,36] and not [34,36]. The elephant starts on p.37 with the tusks, the bronze saddle and the motto that the brain is in the head, not on p.38, which is the leaf given over to its full-page woodcut. And p.42 is deliberately left to the chapter fallback, because the book returns to the horse there, so it resolves to horse without needing a range of its own.

TWO STOPS OUTSIDE THE TICKET'S LIST NEEDED RANGES, to stop the fix creating the very defect it was closing: valley [22,29], because with palm_plain tagged III and standing earlier in the array it would otherwise have won all of chapter III; and portal [43,46], because with horse now tagged IV and standing earlier, the gate's own pages would otherwise have resolved to horse.

SPOT CHECKS, all three from the acceptance criterion, run on the regenerated reading.json: p.19 resolves to great_oak, p.21 to palm_plain, and pp.30-46 to horse 30-34, colossus 35-36, elephant 37-41, horse 42, portal 43-46. horse, colossus and elephant now fire, where before every page of manifest chapter III resolved to valley and every page of IV to portal.

NOT VERIFIED LIVE: reading.json changed substantially, 453 of 463 pages placed, and no browser was loaded this pass, so the Read mode's behaviour on these pages is unconfirmed on the running page.

### `bug-translation-seam-note-wrong` — translation/ says Dallington stops at 'Mustulento' on p.193; he stops at FINIS on p.241

**✅ done** · bug · priority 3 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Found 2026-09-20 closing debt-dallington-tail-unread. Three files in translation/ state the seam wrongly, and they are the files a reader trusts. translation/NOTES.md: 'it stops dead partway through chapter XVII — at the word Mustulento, facsimile page 193 of 467.' translation/manifest.json range.note: 'Dallington's 1592 English covers pages 1-192 and breaks off inside page 193.' translation/en/page_193.md, in its Notes: 'Dallington's translation ends here. What follows is ours... His readers never had Winter, nor anything after.'

All three are false. In the corpus copy of his English, Winter's altar-tag 'Hiemi Æoliæ S.' stands at line 10936, ten lines after Mustulento, so his readers DID have Winter. He then skips 1499 pp.194-237 entirely and resumes at p.238 ('towards the sea side and sandie shore, where we came to an olde decaied temple' = our p.238 word for word), gives the full blazon of Polia (our pp.239-240) and the restraint speech with the Arabian phoenix (our pp.240-241), and closes 'FINIS.' at line 11127 — the end of chapter XVIII, immediately before the argument of chapter XIX. Aligned page by page against translation/en; the match is verbatim at every anchor.

The true statement is: Dallington covers 1499 pp.1-193 continuously and pp.238-241, and nothing between. research/coverage.json now records it (feature xviii-dallington-ends-here); translation/ does not.

**Acceptance.** NOTES.md, manifest.json range.note and the Notes block of translation/en/page_193.md each state the seam correctly: continuous to p.193, a gap over pp.194-237, and a resumption at pp.238-241 ending at FINIS. page_193.md's claim that 'his readers never had Winter' is removed. The CC0 translation itself needs no change — it is the notes about it that are wrong.

**Risk.** The seam note is the project's public account of why this translation exists, and it is quoted in the tour. Getting it wrong understates Dallington by 48 pages in one direction and overstates him by 44 in the other. NOTE: translation/manifest.json was being edited by another session on 2026-09-20 — check git status before touching it.

**Resolution.** Closed 2026-09-20. Re-verified the corpus directly (not just the ticket's account): read Hypnerotomachia_by_Francesco_Colonna.md lines 10900-11140 whole. Confirms Winter's tag 'Hiemi Æoliæ S.' stands ten lines after 'Mustulento Autumno S.', immediately followed by the seaside/old-decayed-temple passage that opens our p.238, then the blazon and restraint speech (Deianira, the tame lions, the ant, the Arabian phoenix), closing 'FINIS.' right before what would be chapter XIX's argument. All three files corrected to state: Dallington continuous to 1499 p.193 (four-Seasons altar complete, Winter included), a gap over pp.194-237, a resumption for four pages at pp.238-241, ending FINIS before chapter XIX. translation/NOTES.md: rewrote the 'Why this exists' paragraph and the COMPLETE-summary paragraph. translation/manifest.json: rewrote range.why and range.note (JSON re-validated). translation/en/page_193.md: rewrote the opening italic seam note, moved and rewrote the inline '(— Dallington's translation ends here...)' aside to sit after the Winter paragraph (where the true break falls) instead of before it, and rewrote the 'The exact seam' Notes bullet, removing 'his readers never had Winter, nor anything after' and replacing with the correct account (his readers never had anything past FINIS at p.241). No translated prose touched. tours.json still repeats the false claim in three places (intro text, the 'triumphs' stop's lede, and the 'venus_temple' stop's lede) even though two other stops in the same file ('priapus'-area notes around chapter XIV/XVII, i.e. the pre-existing 'triumph' notes block and the 'venus_temple' notes list) already state it correctly — filed as bug-tours-dallington-seam-note-wrong rather than edited, since a sibling agent owns tours.json this round.

### `debt-dallington-tail-unread` — Dallington's English runs past the Four Seasons altar to a formal FINIS -- unread and unenumerated

**✅ done** · debt · priority 3 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Found 2026-09-20 while closing bug-tours-prose-ahead-of-geometry. tours.json had told itself Dallington's 1592 English breaks off mid-sentence at 'Mustulento' (facsimile p. 193), and that everything past that point existed in English only under copyright. It does not: in the project's corpus copy, C:\Dev\hypnerotomachia polyphili\md\Hypnerotomachia_by_Francesco_Colonna.md, 'Mustulento Autumno S.' is a complete altar-tag at line 10926, immediately followed by Winter's tag at line 10936, completing the Four Seasons altar. Dallington's English then runs on: the nymph leads Poliphilo 'towards the sea side and sandie shore, where we came to an olde decaied temple' (lines 10937-10947, e-text pp. 256-257), then gives a full blazon of Polia's beauty -- starry forehead, feet, neck with a pearl carkenet, breasts as a 'delicious vallie' -- (lines ~11004-11031, e-text pp. 258-259), and closes with a formal 'FINIS.' at line 11127 (e-text p. 260). The transcriber's own technical notes begin immediately after, at line 11129 ('Technical Notes and further information ... Note that the 1592 English translation covers just under half the Italian text'), confirming this FINIS is the actual end of Dallington's whole 1592 translation, not a chapter break. So there is roughly 200 lines of genuine public-domain 1592 English -- a seaside ruined temple and a complete blazon of Polia -- that this project has never read end-to-end or enumerated into research/coverage.json, and the tour has been telling readers it doesn't exist.

**Acceptance.** An hp-researcher pass reads Hypnerotomachia_by_Francesco_Colonna.md lines 10926-11127 end-to-end against the corresponding 1499 Italian/our translation, enumerates the seaside ruined temple and the blazon of Polia into research/coverage.json chapter by chapter, and records whether either scene is already covered by existing built geometry (the mainland grove, an existing tomb or portrait station) or is a genuine gap.

**Risk.** Closing bug-tours-prose-ahead-of-geometry by editing the Mustulento sentence alone, without opening this ticket, would have buried the fact that this stretch of public-domain English exists and has never been read by this project -- exactly the risk that ticket's own risk note warned against.

**Resolution.** READ END TO END and enumerated — and the tail turns out to be in a different place than the ticket supposed. Corpus md lines 10890-11127 were read whole and aligned page by page against our own translation. Dallington does not merely continue past 'Mustulento': he gives Winter's tag (Hiemi Æoliæ S., line 10936, completing the four Seasons on 1499 p.193), then SKIPS 1499 pp.194-237 ENTIRELY — the Priapus rite, the whole Temple of Venus, the whole of Polia's account of the Polyandrion, about 44 pages — and resumes at 1499 p.238, running to his 'FINIS.' at the end of chapter XVIII, 1499 p.241, immediately before the argument of chapter XIX. So his 1592 English reaches chapter XVIII, not XVII, and the seaside temple and the blazon are NOT chapter XV material as the ledger had them. Enumerated: chapter XVIII gained four entries — xviii-seaside-ruined-temple (re-filed from XV, status raised unbuilt -> PARTIAL: the 'destroyed and deserted temple' on the 'spacious and sandy shore' IS the Polyandrion of ch. XIX, which is built as HPWorldScene._buildPolyandrion; what is missing is the shore, and nothing in build_evidence names a beach, sand or surf), xviii-rest-before-the-temple (the Tempe survey of the whole country from the herbs — the one composed viewpoint in the book, UNBUILT, no station there), xviii-polia-blazon-costume (re-filed from XV and re-read against the 1499: starry forehead vine-tendrilled with gold threads, vermilion shoes moon-mouthed over the ivory instep, the pearl carcanet, the 'delicious little valley' with the sepulchre of his soul beyond Mausolus — UNBUILT, though the book's other blazon at ch. XI is largely built), and xviii-restraint-and-the-exempla (Deianira, the chaste Roman, the lions tamed by time, the ant wearing its path in the flint, the Arabian phoenix, and Polia's face-colour compared to the thrice-changing Tripolion — the book's one explicit refusal, UNBUILT). A fifth entry, xviii-dallington-ends-here, records the edition fact as DECLINED, because tours.json and translation/manifest.json both still tell readers this English does not exist — see ticket bug-translation-seam-note-wrong.

### `debt-plaque-subtitles-too-long` — Twenty-two plaque subtitles are longer than a stone can hold; two lines fixes 21 of them

**✅ done** · debt · priority 3 · hp-builder
 · opened 2026-09-10, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Found 2026-09-10 while looking at the piazza's own ATRIVM plaque, which was running off both ends of the stone. _fitFont shrinks type to a 9 px floor and then stops, so any subtitle longer than about 95 characters was simply CLIPPED -- and nobody had noticed because the clipping happens at both ends symmetrically and still looks like an inscription.

A scan of every `sub:` string under src/scenes/ finds 149 plaques, of which 22 are over 95 characters. The worst is 344 characters (cythera.js, the roses stripped on the day before the Kalends of May); then two at 175 (cythera.js and the glass gardens in approach.js), and a run of them between 115 and 151 in palace.js, temple.js and nature.js.

FIXED IN PART, same day: _plaqueTexture now breaks an over-long subtitle onto TWO lines at the middot nearest the middle, which the inscriptions already carry. That brings 21 of the 22 inside the stone. The 344-character one still overflows, and a few of the 175s are tight. Verified on the running page at the piazza, at Polia's arbour and at the gardens of glass and silk, all three of which were clipped before and read now.

SEPARATE OBSERVATION, not changed and left for Ted: the plaque canvas is 320x96 for a `wide` plaque and the plane it maps onto is typically 4.6 x 0.5, which is 9.2:1 against the canvas's 3.33:1 -- so ALL plaque lettering in this world is stretched horizontally by about 2.8x. Widening the canvas would unstretch it and fit more characters at once, but it changes the look of all 149 plaques, so it is a directional call and not a fix to make quietly.

RE-MEASURED 2026-09-20, and the 'few of the 175s are tight' note undersold it badly: measured against this project's own Georgia with canvas.measureText (not a character-count guess), EIGHTEEN of the twenty-two over-95-character subtitles still overran the stone at the 9px floor after the two-line middot split, not just the 344-character (329 once its \u00b7 escapes resolve) Cythera rose plaque this ticket named. Only cythera.js:1586, palace.js:995 and temple.js:451 genuinely fit as two lines. The other eighteen -- cythera.js:232,494,870; palace.js:399,424,444,458,493,508,1261,1739,1889,2260; temple.js:516,555; nature.js:212,1291 -- were all still clipping quietly, exactly the failure mode this ticket describes, just undercounted.

**Acceptance.** No plaque subtitle is clipped at either end at the distance its station stands at: every `sub:` string under src/scenes/ either fits one line or splits into two that each fit. Check the 344-character Cythera rose plaque, which currently does not.

**Resolution.** DONE, and wider than the ticket's own acceptance example. The fix is entirely inside materials.js -- _plaqueLines and the two-line render path are untouched for plaques that already fit, so cythera.js, palace.js, temple.js and nature.js needed no edits at all.

WHAT CHANGED. _plaqueTexture now checks the middot-split lines' actual measured width at the 9px floor (`x.measureText`) instead of trusting the split to have worked. When it hasn't -- which, re-measured, is most of the over-95-character subtitles, not only the named outlier -- it falls back to a new _plaqueWrapLines (plain greedy word-wrap via the new _wrapWords helper), trying three lines and then four at the 9px floor before touching the floor itself, and lowering it only as far as the one plaque that still needs it: the Cythera rose plaque (our pp. 375-376), which needed all four lines at 6px (it ran to seven lines at 9px). The lines render evenly spaced between the title and the border (y 56-88) rather than at the old fixed two-line y's, so one/two/three/four-line plaques all sit centred in the room the title leaves them.

VERIFIED, on the running page, two ways. (1) Called the live, deployed `sc._plaqueTexture()` (materials.js?v=10, confirmed loaded via the script tag) with the exact 329-character rose subtitle and appended its output canvas to the DOM: four lines, fully legible, comfortably inside the plaque's border, matching the fix's design. (2) Ran all 21 of the over-95-character subtitles (every one `grep`-found across cythera.js, palace.js, temple.js and nature.js) through the live `sc._plaqueLines` / `sc._plaqueWrapLines` and measured every resulting line's width against the 298px inner width at its rendered font size: zero overflow, all 21. Also stood the walker in-world at the Cythera rose plaque's actual world position (its parent group offsets local Z by -7285.4, which the first placement attempt missed) and saw the plaque's title and the start of its wrapped subtitle rendered in the scene itself, bounded by the plaque's own dark field, not running past it -- the rest of the plaque was obscured by the sepulchre's own backlit alabaster figure (by the book's own design, 'burning unsteadily by the light set opposite', our p.373) and garden foliage in this camera position, which is a framing/occlusion matter, not a text-fit one; the direct canvas call is the conclusive check for fit.

THE 175-CHARACTER ONES: checked, and neither was actually a clean two-line fit -- cythera.js:870 (165 chars, the Adonis distich) now renders as three lines at 9px, not two; the ticket's second '175' (the glass garden, approach.js -- out of this ticket's file scope, and separately confirmed already fitting at 92 characters, one line) was never in danger. Two subtitles the ticket didn't single out (cythera.js:1586, palace.js:995, temple.js:451) were already genuine two-line fits and are untouched by this change -- confirmed by re-measuring them, not assumed.

CACHE CHAIN bumped: materials.js v9->10 (src/scenes/HPWorldScene.js:45), HPWorldScene.js v317->318 (src/main.js:6), main.js v423->424 (src/index.html:1371). Parse-checked with `node --check` on all three touched .js files.

NOT CHANGED, per the ticket's own note and this brief's scope: the plaque canvas dimensions (320x96) and the plane aspect ratio (9.2:1 vs the canvas's 3.33:1) are untouched -- still Ted's call, not made quietly here.

hpDiag(): this is a canvas-2D text-layout change only -- no geometry, material or mesh is added, removed or resized, so draw calls/meshes/triangles are architecturally unaffected. Read after the change (this session never captured a pre-edit reading, since the fix was designed and measured with standalone prototype canvases before it was written into materials.js; a repeat reading immediately after was byte-identical to the first, confirming no frame-to-frame drift at this camera position): drawCalls 1430, meshes 6590, geometries 6580, materials 3350, triangles 4381680, fps ~1.9 (this preview session's fps is far under the project's stated ~26fps baseline generally, consistent with the dev-preview sandbox's renderer rather than with this change -- draw-call and mesh counts, which a canvas-text change cannot move, are the relevant regression check here and are unaffected).

### `debt-reading-station-is-chapter-grained` — The reading mode places a page by its CHAPTER, so a long chapter strands the reader at one station

**✅ done** · debt · priority 3 · hp-builder
 · opened 2026-09-09, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Noticed 2026-09-09 while fixing bug-chapter-xi-tour-misattributed, and it is the same weakness one level down. build_reading.py's chapter_to_station() takes the FIRST stop of each chapter and every page of that chapter inherits it. Chapter X runs 1499 pp. 117-140 -- twenty-four pages -- and its first stop in the array is #14, "The Palace, the Water-Labyrinth and the Banquet", tagged IX-X. So the chess ballet at p. 119 puts the reader at the WATER LABYRINTH while the text describes thirty-two girls dancing on a chequered pavement, and the world has a Human Chess Match station (#15) standing built and unused for exactly that text.

This is not a mis-tag -- both stops are correctly chapter X. It is that the page->station map has no resolution below a chapter, and the chapters in this book are long.

Verified live at main.js?v=382: reading.json p. 119 resolves to `labyrinth`, p. 141 to `polia`. Re-verified 2026-09-20 before this fix, directly against the regenerated-but-not-yet-fixed reading.json (main.js's DATA_V had since moved to 48; behaviour was unchanged): p.119 still `labyrinth`, p.141 still `polia`.

**Acceptance.** A tour stop can declare the 1499 PAGE RANGE it covers, and reading.json resolves each page to the narrowest stop that contains it, falling back to the chapter rule when no stop declares a range. Checked on p. 119, which must resolve to `chess`, and on p. 141, which must stay `polia`.

**Resolution.** Five chapter-X stops (labyrinth, chess, artificial, quinta_essentia, three_doors) each gained a "pages": [lo, hi] field in tours.json, read off translation/en/page_*.md directly rather than the tour prose: labyrinth 92-118 (the palace tour and the banquet, closing with a full page of recap -- 'who would believe with what luxury' -- that is still praising the banquet, not yet the game); chess 119-121 (p.119: 'she ordered a game to be looked at...an excellent dance' and the thirty-two girls enter; the third dance's winner is declared partway through p.121); artificial 122-127 (the queen names Logistica and Thelemia at p.122, they walk him out to the glass garden at p.123-124, and the water-labyrinth Logistica narrates from its watch-tower runs to the 'let us go down to our companion Thelemia' at the end of p.127 -- note this water-labyrinth is the SAME one tours.json's own `labyrinth`-stop lede describes, but it is narrated here, later, not during the p.92-118 palace tour: the tour write-up compresses two textual locations into one lede, which is fine for prose but was not fine for a page range, so the range follows the text, not the lede); quinta_essentia 128-134 (Thelemia's song, then the triangular obelisk with its genii and hieroglyphs, ending with Logistica's gloss 'these hieroglyphs...are most fitly set here as a monument for those passing by' at p.134); three_doors 135-140 (the titles above the doors, the three ladies, and Logistica breaking her lute at p.139, closing the chapter at p.140). build_reading.py's chapter_to_station() was left alone and renamed page_to_station_ranges()/station_for_page() added beside it: ranges are checked narrowest-first, falling back to the chapter rule for every chapter that still has only one stop. Regenerated reading.json confirms both named checks (p.119 chess, p.141 polia) and every page 92-140 now resolves within the five ranges with no gap. SWEPT for the same shape elsewhere: chapters I (3 stops: plain/wood/great_oak), II (2 stops: wood/palm_plain) and III (4 stops: horse/colossus/elephant x2) each have the identical first-stop-wins defect -- confirmed live in the regenerated reading.json, e.g. all of manifest chapter III (pp.20-29) still resolves to `valley` and all of chapter IV (pp.30-46) to `portal`, so `horse`/`colossus`/`elephant` never fire at all. NOT fixed here: these five stops carry "half": "dallington" chapter tags, and a text check found the mismatch runs deeper than a resolution gap -- the Palm-grove-and-wolf text tours.json's `palm_plain` stop (tagged chapter II) describes is actually on p.21, which translation/manifest.json calls chapter III, and the Great-Oak sleep tours.json's `great_oak` stop (tagged chapter I) describes is on p.19, chapter II. Adding page ranges under a chapter tag that is itself wrong would be inventing a boundary, not citing one, so this is filed as debt-early-chapter-tags-drift-from-1499-pagination instead of guessed at here. Not touched: src/main.js's DATA_V (still '48') was not bumped -- out of scope for this pass -- so the regenerated reading.json is not yet live; the reading mode's page-to-station text needs both a DATA_V bump and a browser check (walk to p.119 in Read mode and confirm the world stands at the chess station, not the water-labyrinth) before this is verified end to end.

**Files.** `scripts/build_reading.py` · `src/data/tours.json` · `src/data/reading.json`

**See.** ticket bug-chapter-xi-tour-misattributed · COVERAGE.md ch. X · ticket bug-early-chapter-tags-drift-from-1499-pagination

**✅ done** · debt · priority 3 · hp-builder

The off-by-one is handled explicitly: METALS[7] does not exist, so above Sol the target is WEDDING. Verified on the running page at localhost:3458 on a worktree carrying exactly this change: r = 5.0 gave '☿ Quicksilver — 5.0 / 7.5 m'; r = 12 gave '☉ Gold — 12.0 / 18.0 m' with no NaN and no 'undefined'; r = 0.22 gives '♄ Lead — 0.22 / 0.60 m'.

### `roll-shed-by-area` — The crust sheds by count, not by surface area

**✅ done** · debt · priority 3 · hp-builder
 · opened 2026-09-09, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** tune.crust is a flat 2000 whatever the ball's size. The honest rule is that a ball has 4*pi*R^2 of surface and only so many things fit on it, so a small ball should carry few and a huge one thousands -- which is the density curve Katamari's visuals actually follow. Explained in full in CRUST.md. The arithmetic: a sphere's surface goes as R squared, so from 0.3 m to 12 m the radius grows 40-fold and the area 1600-fold, while the cap of 2000 THINGS does not move -- 2000 objects on 1810 square metres is bare. The ball therefore gets balder the bigger it gets, which is backwards. The replacement dial is `crustLayers`, how many layers deep the heap is, which is a number a person can picture.

**Acceptance.** The crust sheds when the summed cross-section of what is stuck exceeds a multiple of 4*pi*R^2; a 0.5 m ball carries visibly fewer things than a 6 m one.

**Resolution.** _swallow's shed loop (RollUp.js) now sheds on summed cross-section, not count alone: `used = sum(pi*size^2)` over `_stuck`, `room = 4*pi*r^2*tune.crustLayers` (new dial, default 3, CRUST.md's own guess -- not yet swept and confirmed by measurement, live-tunable at roll.tune.crustLayers same as camBase/camScale), and the while sheds (smallest of the sixty oldest, unchanged) while `used > room` OR the count exceeds `tune.crust` (2000, kept as the absolute backstop CRUST.md #6.3 asked for, so a very large ball still can't try to draw an unbounded count). Verified on the running page (localhost:3457/src/index.html, main.js?v=415): entered roll mode, then for each of roll.r = 0.5 and roll.r = 6 fed 5000 synthetic 0.15 m edibles through the real _swallow path with r pinned after each call (so growth didn't confound the reading) and read `_stuck.length` after. 0.5 m ball settled at 133 stuck (used 9.40 m^2 against room 9.42 m^2 -- the area rule bound first, matching CRUST.md #4's own worked table of ~130 at 3 layers/0.15 m average); the 6 m ball settled at 2000 (used only 141 m^2 against a room of 1357 m^2 -- the count backstop bound first, as CRUST.md #4 predicts happens once the area-implied cap runs into the tens of thousands). So the 6 m ball carries 15x what the 0.5 m ball carries, satisfying the acceptance criterion directly. Cache chain bumped cleanly: both of RollUp.js's other importers (scenes/HPWorldScene.js, scenes/world/rollup.js) were untouched by any other in-progress session at the time, so the chain went RollUp.js?v=11->12, world/rollup.js?v=10->11 (its import line changed), HPWorldScene.js?v=308->309 (ditto), main.js?v=414->415 in src/index.html. hpDiag() read 162 draw calls on a fresh roll-mode entry both before and after the synthetic test (cleaned up after), and the new shed rule can only ever hold LESS OR EQUAL crust than the old flat 2000 cap at every radius the area rule binds, so no regression is possible by construction.

**Files.** `src/systems/RollUp.js`

**See.** ROLLING.md#3


### `tr-confidence-unstated-180` — 180 of 463 englished pages carry no stated confidence at all

**✅ done** · debt · priority 3 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Follow-on from tr-verified-overclaims (closed 2026-09-20), which fixed the badge's wording but not the underlying gap it exposed: of 463 pages, the confidence census reads high 48, medium 232, low 3, UNSTATED 180 (scripts/translation_status.py --next 0). Those 180 pages have a translation and carry no [?...] markers, so they show the "no queries" badge (post-fix) with no confidence pill value beside it -- a reader still cannot tell whether the translator was in fact confident or simply never wrote the **Confidence:** line the other 283 pages carry.

**Acceptance.** Every one of the 180 pages listed by `python scripts/translation_status.py` under confidence unstated is read against the facsimile (or the translator's own working notes, where the judgement was simply never transcribed) and given a stated high/medium/low **Confidence:** line, so that a re-run of translation_status.py reports 0 unstated among drafted+verified pages.

**Resolution.** DONE, all 180. `python scripts/translation_status.py` now reports `confidence high 58 low 5 medium 400` and NO `unstated` among the 463 drafted+verified pages, where before this pass it read `high 47 low 3 medium 233 unstated 180`. The reviewer line at the foot of the report is down from 183 pages to five: 135, 164, 300, 303, 304.

WHERE THE 180 WERE, AND WHY THEY HAD NO LINE. They are a contiguous block, pages 11 to 192 (less the blank leaves 55 and 90) -- chapters I to XVII, the half of the book Dallington covers. They were englished in the whole-book pass of 2026-09-08/09 (commits d56dd00 and a55bdd0), begun because Ted wanted a full English Hypnerotomachia to listen to "with no apparatus and no seam". They were written to that brief: not one of the 180 carried a `## Notes` section at all, so there was no confidence line to omit. The judgement was genuinely never made rather than never transcribed, which is why this had to be a reading pass and not a transcription one.

METHOD. Each page was read as a pair, `translation/source/page_NNN.txt` beside `translation/en/page_NNN.md`, all 180 of them, and graded against the rubric `translation/NOTES.md` already states and the 283 scored pages already practise -- high for plain narrative or Latin with allusions identified and nothing structural guessed; medium where the sense is secure but something was compromised (a period broken up, technical vocabulary given by its standard equivalent, a passage rendered literally rather than smoothed); low where something is genuinely unresolved. NOTES.md says to be generous with medium and the existing corpus bears that out (47 high against 233 medium), so medium is the default and high is earned. The new distribution follows the old one closely: 11 high, 167 medium, 2 low. Each note names the page's content, then says what is secure and where a reviewer should start, and each carries a dated line saying the confidence was stated by a second reader and not by the translator, so nobody later mistakes these for the translator's own self-assessment. Godwin 1999 was not opened, quoted or paraphrased at any point.

THE TWO LOW PAGES, both of which need work beyond a confidence line. (1) PAGE 135, the worst gap found: the three doors' titles are missing and the page does not say so. The source transcription for that leaf is not text but a Wikisource image-map stub (`File:Hypnerotomachia_Poliphili_pag135.jpg`, `rect` co-ordinates, the transcriber's note *caratteri a caso!*), because the titles are cut in the woodcut. The English says only that Poliphilo "saw the title that the divine Queen Eleuterylida had foretold" and prints none of the three, with no editorial note -- so the three names on which the whole three-doors chapter turns have silently dropped out, and the door-scenes on pp. 136-138 are unlabelled. (2) PAGE 164, Apollo's oracle on the second triumph: the Italian gives two Latin clauses that look alike and mean differently, `Uni gratum mare. Alterum gratum mari.`, and says in the same breath that the answer was *perplexibelmente* and *ambiguo*. The English prints "the one is pleasing to the sea; the other is pleasing to the sea" -- the same clause twice -- and drops the Latin, so the reader is told an answer is ambiguous and shown one that is merely repetitive.

WHAT THE READING TURNED UP BESIDES. Four patterns run through the block and are recorded page by page in the notes; each is a candidate for its own ticket rather than for this one.

(a) THE INSCRIPTIONS ARE SYSTEMATICALLY REPLACED BY THEIR TRANSLATIONS. Where the 1499 carves Greek, Latin or Hebrew, the bulk pass usually prints only an English line and drops the original: TEMPUS and AMISSIO (p. 34), the hieroglyph-reading EX LABORE DEO NATURAE SACRIFICA (p. 41), NIHIL FIRMUM (p. 49), the frieze dedication with Colonna's own Latin gloss (p. 52), ΔΙΟΣ ΑΙΓΙΟΧΟΙΟ (p. 54), ΑΕΙ ΣΠΕΥΔΕ ΒΡΑΔΕΩΣ / Semper festina tarde on the Aldine device itself (pp. 69, 75), ΠΑΝΤΩΝ ΤΟΚΑΔΙ (p. 73), the trilingual epitaphs in the elephant (pp. 39, 40), NEMO (p. 159), ΣΥ ΜΟΙ ΓΛΥΚΥΣ ΤΕ ΚΑΙ ΠΙΚΡΟΣ (p. 169), the monostich the text itself announces as carved on a tablet (p. 172), Herbam do (p. 150), and the Vertumnus trophy (p. 191). The same pages elsewhere do it correctly -- GENEA, ASAMINTHOS, GELOIASTOS, AMALTHEA, MELISSA, Cerebrum est in capite, and both bridge-mottoes on p. 134 are kept and glossed -- so this is unevenness, not policy. The sharpest demonstration is at the seam: p. 192 gives `Florido veri. S.` as "sacred to the flowering spring", and p. 193, three sentences later and the first page of the annotated translation, sets the other three faces of the same altar as block quotations with the Latin kept.

(b) SEVERAL PAGES END WITH A DANGLING COLON where an inscription is missing from the source and nothing says so: the second pedestal roundel (p. 33, whose readings hp.db `woodcut_catalog` nos. 7 and 8 actually record as D.AMBIG.D.D. and Equus infalicitatis), the elephant's saddle-cloth (p. 37, catalogue no. 11), and the first bridge-panel (p. 69).

(c) THE ALLEGORICAL NAMES ARE TRANSLITERATED AND NEVER GLOSSED, so the schemes they encode are invisible in English: the five nymphs at the bath are the five senses and each carries her own sense's attribute in the same sentence (p. 79); Cynosia, Indalomena and Mnemosyna are the three inner faculties one passes in order (p. 93); Logistica and Thelemia are Reason and Will and Telosia is the End (p. 122); and the attendants at the three doors are the contemplative, active and voluptuous virtues (pp. 136-138). On p. 180 the singers before the four cars are the mistresses of Latin love-elegy, Lycoris, Nemesis, Delia, Corinna, Cynthia, Quintilia, Violantilla and the rest, with Catullus's Lesbia present as "the other weeping for the sparrow", and not one poet is named.

(d) A HANDFUL OF FLAT ERRORS, each named on its page: `bombicina` given as "cotton" where it is the sheerest silk, on p. 143 in the same sentence as Pamphila the inventress of Coan SILK (and again p. 75); Nicomedes made king of the Cnidians instead of Bithynia (p. 71); Cadmus's brothers made Europa's sons, and Thebes called Athens (p. 60); `scalina` read as a stairway where Colonna glosses it himself as a scalene triangle (p. 46); `demeritamente` inverted to "undeservedly" (p. 66, and correctly rendered "the thanks I owe" on p. 79); Arsinoe made queen of Arabia (p. 131); Leda made daughter of Theseus (p. 166); Circe's transformations attributed to Calypso (p. 185); the gold that is "the deadly poison of virtue and peace" attached to fire instead (p. 162); `Mixe` rendered banana on p. 74 and mallow on p. 190; a clause of p. 182 missing from the English altogether; and the pawn's move on p. 120 rendered as a rule no piece could obey. Page 92's heading also reads Chapter IX where 93 reverts to VIII and the rubric does not fall until 94 -- and because the manifest takes each page's chapter from its own heading, that error is in the manifest too.

SCOPE AND WHAT WAS NOT TOUCHED. This pass added confidence lines and notes only; not one word of any translation was changed, and no `[?...]` marker was inserted, so the drafted/verified census is exactly what it was (12 drafted, 451 verified). `translation/manifest.json` is deliberately not committed, as in tr-front-matter-review: its confidence field is derived and the next run of scripts/translation_status.py regenerates it. No hpDiag or live-page verification applies -- research/translation.html is generated but is not reachable from the deployed HP world, and this change has no rendering surface; it was verified by re-running scripts/translation_status.py and reading the census.

**Files.** `translation/en/` · `scripts/translation_status.py`

**See.** translation/NOTES.md


### `tr-front-matter-review` — The ten front-matter pages have never been read by anyone but their translator

**✅ done** · debt · priority 3 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-09, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Pages 1-10 were translated 2026-09-09 from the Wikisource transcription of the 1499 Aldine. Four readings are marked [?...] and explained in the notes (Crasso's `quo nam pacto me tibi aperiam`, `audaculus`, the Bibbiena siege, and Marone's run-together `quid eritnoscetur`). The other six pages carry no flagged doubt, which under this project's definition makes them `verified` -- and that word means only 'no marker left', not 'checked against the facsimile by a second reader'.

**Acceptance.** Someone other than the translator reads pages 1-10 against the facsimile and either clears the four marked readings or replaces them with better ones.

**Resolution.** READ by a second reader, all ten pages, against the 1499 facsimile -- Siena, Biblioteca Comunale degli Intronati, O.III.38, ff. 1r-5v, in the read-only corpus at 'site/images/siena/'. Folio-to-page mapping confirmed by opening every leaf: our page N is folio ceil(N/2) recto (odd N) or verso (even N), so pages 1-10 are ff. 1r, 1v, 2r, 2v, 3r, 3v, 4r, 4v, 5r, 5v. Godwin 1999 was not opened, quoted or paraphrased at any point; nothing in the corpus is Godwin.

THE FOUR FLAGGED READINGS. Three confirmed, one confirmed and improved; all four markers cleared from the text. (1) Crasso's 'quo nam pacto me tibi aperiam' (p.2) CONFIRMED -- the facsimile reads exactly as the transcription does, and the decisive evidence is the next sentence, 'literis aditum ad te tanquam vadum tentavi', which continues the same metaphor of access: Crasso is looking for a way in, so 'open myself to you' is right and 'commend myself' would lose the image. (2) 'audaculus' (p.2) CONFIRMED and printed plainly ('in cuius nomen audaculus prodiret'); it is a -culus diminutive of audax and an adjective of the book, not an adverb, so the English is changed from 'a little more boldly' to 'a little bolder'; the surrounding figure (parente orbatus, veluti pupillus sine tutela) fixes the sense. (3) The Bibbiena siege (p.2): the PLACE is certain -- the facsimile reads 'Bibienae', and that is the Latin for Bibbiena in the Casentino -- so the marker is cleared, but the first pass's gloss was wrong on the EVENT and is corrected: the siege belongs to the Casentino campaign of 1498 and Guidobaldo was then in VENETIAN service, not Florentine, which is also why a Veronese served under his auspices. Nothing in this corpus documents that campaign, so the note now says so in terms and records the one lead the corpus does give (Trippe, Renaissance Quarterly 55.4, note 3, citing Oettinger 15-46, which is not on this machine). (4) Marone's 'quid eritnoscetur' (p.8) CONFIRMED, and it turns out never to have been a conjecture at all: the 1499 PUNCTUATES it. Aldus's question mark in this fount appears five times in the same eight lines (after musa, Vestrum, titulus, Poliphilus, cur), and it stands between 'erit' and 'noscetur' and again after 'sin minus'. The Wikisource transcriber dropped an unfamiliar glyph; the printer's own division is 'Si parcet, quid erit? noscetur. sin minus? haud uos ...'. The English is improved with it: 'quid erit' is the idiom 'what then?', not 'what will he be?'.

WHAT THE UNFLAGGED PAGES TURNED UP -- two mistranslations and one unflagged doubt, none of them visible without reading the Latin. (a) PAGE 8, the second epigram, the worst of them: the last line had agent and patient reversed. 'Te dum Poliphilus somno iacet obrutus alto, / Pervigilare facit docta per ora virum' was rendered 'you make the man keep watch, through learned lips', making Polia the actor. Te is accusative and cannot be the subject of facit, and virum is the syncopated genitive plural of vir in the tag 'per ora virum' (Ennius's epitaph 'volito vivus per ora virum'; Virgil, Georgics 3.9) -- the standard Latin figure for outliving death by being spoken of. It reads: while Poliphilo lies buried in sleep, HE keeps HER awake, in the learned mouths of men. That is what the couplet above it promises (vivis mortua, sed melius) and it restores the book's own somno/pervigilare pun. Corrected. (b) PAGE 4, the last couplet of the anonymous elegy: 'Annua per Venerem, Naiadasque leges' had been read twice over, as both the verb leges and the noun leges, producing 'yearly by Venus -- and you shall read the Naiads' laws', and there are no Naiads' laws in the book. The facsimile puts the comma after Venerem, so per governs both nouns and leges is the future of lego: you will read what annual rites are kept at Adonis's tomb by Venus and the Naiads. The proof is internal and contemporary -- the Italian terza rima on p.7, which is this same elegy translated in 1499, reads 'celebrato gli e lo anniversario / per le Naiade e Venus mischinella'. Corrected. (c) PAGE 7, NEW FLAG: 'a questo evinto', of the fountain of the Paphian, was translated literally and silently as 'conquered by this'. Two readings are open -- evinto from evincere (overcome) or evinto for avvinto (bound to) -- and only the second fits the topography, since the Fountain of Venus stands in the middle of the theatre. Now marked '[?joined to this]' with both readings argued, and page 7 drops from confidence high to medium and from verified to drafted. It is the only marker left in pages 1-10.

SMALLER FINDS, all from the facsimile and all fixed in the notes: the 1499 sets ATQVE OBITER as one word on both title pages (the transcription splits it 'ob iter'); the privilege's last word is broken IMPPRIME/RE with a doubled p, which modern texts normalise away; p.9's tapering block is EIGHT lines, not the six the notes claimed; p.3's 'summo ... Polo' is heaven, not 'the highest Pole', as the vernacular version's 'dal ciel demissi' proves, and the English is changed; p.8 line 2 had dropped 'Vestrum?' ('Yours?'), restored; p.3's Scita line 8 prints 'sed' where Pozzi-Ciapponi emend to 'se<u>', now recorded with the emendation attributed to them and the wording ours; p.1's confidence line said 'nine words of Latin' for nineteen. The Siena copy also carries a contemporary marginal gloss 'Pugna Amoris' beside the half-title on f.5r -- the earliest reading of the title we can watch happening -- noted on p.9 as copy-specific.

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, and is now said on the page instead of being left silent: the identity of the Bibbiena campaign (inference from Guidobaldo's career, not sourced in this corpus), and 'a questo evinto' (would need a fifteenth-century Venetian lexicon we do not have). Every one of the ten pages now opens its Notes with a dated second-reader line naming the folio checked, so 'read by someone other than the translator' is a recorded fact and not an inference from an absent marker -- which is the distinction sibling ticket tr-verified-overclaims exists to fix, and which this ticket does not pretend to have fixed. translation/manifest.json is deliberately NOT updated (out of scope for this pass): its status field is derived, so the next run of scripts/translation_status.py will move page 7 to drafted and pages 2 and 8 to verified by itself. No live-page verification applies -- this is a translation and research-ledger change with no rendering surface.

### `tr-verified-overclaims` — "verified" in the translation manifest means less than it sounds

**✅ done** · infra · priority 3 · hp-builder
 · opened 2026-09-09, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** translation_status.py sets status=verified for any page with no [?...] markers left. 450 of 463 pages carry that label. The legend in the script and the paragraph on the parallel-text page both define it correctly, but the word on the green badge does not, and the confidence census tells the real story: high 48, medium 232, low 3, UNSTATED 180.

**Acceptance.** Either the badge is renamed to what it measures (`no queries`, say), or every page carries a stated confidence so the badge and the census cannot disagree.

**Resolution.** Renamed the badge, not the manifest. The manifest's internal status field ("verified" = no [?...] marker left) and the script's docstring legend were already correct, and the Method paragraph on research/translation.html already stated the criterion correctly in prose -- the ticket's own evidence said so. What overclaimed was the two-letter word rendered on the per-page green pill, read alone, without the paragraph above it. build_translation_page.py now renders that pill as "no queries" (class .badge.clear) instead of "verified", and the Method paragraph's own sentence was rewritten to name the badge by its new word and to say explicitly that it is not the same claim as the confidence pill beside it. Verified by rebuilding: page 12 (confidence: unstated, one of the 180) now shows badge "no queries" next to pill "confidence: unstated" -- no page can show a badge that claims a check the confidence pill denies. `grep -c 'badge verified' research/translation.html` is 0; `grep -c 'no queries'` is 451 (450 pages + the one instance in the Method paragraph's own example). Option (b) -- giving all 180 UNSTATED pages a real confidence judgement -- was considered and declined for this pass: it requires reading each page against the facsimile, the same second-reader work tr-front-matter-review already asks for on 10 pages, at eighteen times the size. Doing it badly (rubber-stamping a confidence level without reading the page) would leave the badge lying in a different way, so it is filed as its own ticket (tr-confidence-unstated-180) for a future research pass rather than half-done here. No hpDiag applies: research/translation.html is generated but is not part of the deployed HP world (it is not reachable from src/index.html or main.js, and the 3-D site reads no translation-manifest data), so there is no live-site rendering surface to verify against; the fix was verified by rebuilding the static page and grepping the output, per the task's own instruction on when hpDiag does not apply.

**Evidence.** Opened 2026-09-20 closing bug-plate-images-bound-to-page-seq-plus-eight. With the offset corrected to +10 the plate count bound into reading.json falls from 162 to 159. The three that drop out are pp.55, 90 and 195, and they drop because build_reading.py skips any manifest page whose status is 'blank' (and any page with no translation/en/ file, which these also lack). Their manifest entries say 'Source page is empty (0 bytes). A blank leaf in the facsimile; nothing to translate.' That is wrong about what they are: coverage_seed.py's measurement note records 55 / 90 / 195 as page_seq 45 / 80 / 185, which are catalogue #23 the gate with the medallion busts, the third fountain, and #71 the worship of Priapus -- the one full-page cut of the temple sequence and the book's most explicit image, the leaf Benedetto Giovio noted was cut out of some copies. They have no text because they are entirely picture. Under the old +8 these three cuts appeared, two pages early, on pp.53, 88 and 193; they are now correctly named and invisible. p.380, the fourth such 'blank', is a genuine blank leaf before the Book II title page and has no plate.

**Acceptance.** Reading mode shows a page 55, 90 and 195, each carrying its own plate and an editorial line saying the leaf is a full-page woodcut; manifest.json distinguishes a full-page-woodcut leaf from a blank one (a status of its own, or a note that build_reading.py reads); and reading.json binds 162 plates, not 159.

**Risk.** Touches the manifest's status vocabulary, which coverage_seed.py and translation_status.py also read -- check both before adding a value. The page count in reading.json's report will change, so the number quoted in build_reading.py's docstring should change with it.

**Resolution.** Closed 2026-09-20. All three scans were opened before anything was written, and all three are picture to the frame with no body text: p.55 (page_seq 45) the great gate — a pedimented aedicule, paired Corinthian columns on high pedestals, a medallion bust in each spandrel, a Greek inscription across the pediment, catalogue #16, the only ink outside the frame being the signature; p.90 (page_seq 80) the tiered fountain — lipped basin, three winged sphinx-figures under the lower bowl, a second bowl ringed with lion masks and dragon heads, a double figure at the top throwing the jets, catalogue #23, the only ink outside the frame being the catchword; p.195 (page_seq 185) the worship of Priapus — the herm on its altar under a leafy bower hung with lamps, nymphs and men with lighted torches, the garlanded ass led up with basin and knife, catalogue #71. p.380 was also checked and IS a genuine blank leaf, the turn before the Book II title page, and stays skipped.

MECHANISM. A status of its own was the obvious move and is the wrong one: `status` is DERIVED from disk by scripts/translation_status.py, whose reconcile() writes 'blank' for any page whose Italian source is zero bytes, so a hand-set status would be silently reverted on the next run. translation_status.py was out of scope. So manifest.json gains `leaf` instead — 'full-page-woodcut' or 'blank' — hand-maintained beside the derived status and documented in a new `leaf_values` block. It survives a reconcile because reconcile() only ever writes status, en_words, uncertain and confidence. Each of the three also gains a reader-facing `note` describing what is on the leaf, and a `leaf_basis` naming the scan opened; build_reading.py emits a woodcut leaf with an empty body, its plate and that note as the editorial line, so a future such leaf is a data change and not a code change. The two wrong confidence_notes ('A blank leaf in the facsimile; nothing to translate') are gone and range.note no longer calls all four blank.

RESULT: reading.json 463 -> 466 pages and 159 -> 162 plates, which is the acceptance criterion. The three new records resolve to stations portal, court and priapus. build_translation_page.py and translation_status.py were both read before the value was added, as the risk note asked, and neither needed changing: both test `status == 'blank'`, which these pages still are. NOT VERIFIED IN A BROWSER — no live-page check was available in this pass and src/main.js (DATA_V) was out of scope, so a returning reader keeps the cached reading.json until that bump: infra-data-v-not-bumped-for-plate-reoffset.

**Files.** `translation/manifest.json` · `scripts/build_reading.py` · `src/data/reading.json`

Read mode raises a plate frame on each of them, so the reader is shown a photograph of a page of solid type presented as this leaf's woodcut. NOTE the converse gap in the same measurement: the corrected catalogue puts cuts on our pp.191, 192, 193, 194 and 306 — the Triumph of Vertumnus and Pomona and the Four Seasons reliefs among them — for which images/woodcuts_1499/ holds NO file at all, so those cuts cannot come up in Read mode however the binding is fixed.

Separately, the five leaves the catalogue places cuts on but for which no image exists (191-194, 306) are either fetched from the corpus or recorded, with a reason, as unavailable.

**Risk.** Do not infer the answer from the absence of a catalogue row — the catalogue is itself only good to about two pages and this pass found rows misplaced in both directions. **Resolution.** DONE, both halves. FALSE FRAMES: build_reading.py no longer binds a plate by the existence of images/woodcuts_1499/pNNN.jpg. plate_captions() now returns a `has_cut` set beside the captions, and a leaf is bound only if its scan was opened and a cut seen, or — for leaves nobody has opened — if a catalogue row resolves to it. reading.json falls from 162 plates to 149; the 18 suppressed leaves are 48, 94, 161, 180, 185, 190, 200, 210, 250, 268, 270, 280, 337, 399, 402, 425, 445, 459, and EVERY ONE of them was opened on the scan first, per this ticket's own risk note. pp.48, 94 and 161 specifically no longer raise a frame; asserted in the JSON, not inferred.

THE 38-LEAF LIST WAS NOT THE ANSWER, IN EITHER DIRECTION, and this is the finding. Of the 38 leaves the ticket named as having a file and no catalogue row, TWENTY-FOUR carry a real woodcut and keep their plate: 167 (the elephants of the second triumph, running head SECVNDVS), 172, 174, 214, 229, 232, 234, 238, 244, 252, 254, 256, 258, 263, 267, 269, 271, 301, 317, 338, 345, 346, 401 and 431. A list derived from a jittery catalogue is a place to start looking, not a verdict; 72 leaves were opened to settle it.

THE CONVERSE GAP IS FETCHED, NOT RECORDED UNAVAILABLE. pp.191-194 and 306 now have plates. The corpus holds a SECOND complete facsimile at staging\ia_scan\nNNN.jpg — 299 leaves, n175-n473, all 4659x7086 — calibrated at n = page_seq + 5, measured by opening n190 (the full-page Priapus = page_seq 185 = our p.195) and n186 (the Vertumnus car with its INTEGERRIMAM CORPOR. ### `bug-tours-triumphs-xv-stop-is-chapter-xvii` — tours.json's Vertumnus and Pomona stop is tagged chapter XV but describes chapter XVII, and chapter XVI is left with no tour stop at all

**✅ done** · bug · priority 4 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Found 2026-09-20 closing bug-tours-priapus-stop-chapter-tag and bug-early-chapter-tags-drift-from-1499-pagination, which between them show this is the same defect at a third seam. The 'triumphs' stop titled 'Vertumnus and Pomona' is tagged chapter XV. Its content is chapter XVII: the car of Vertumnus and Pomona is our pp.190-191 and the four-sided Seasons altar pp.192-194, every one of those pages headed Chapter XVII, and the ledger already files them there as xvii-vertumnus-pomona-triumph, xvii-seasons-altar and xvii-seasons-altar-inscriptions. The five plates were measured onto page_seq 181-184 = our pp.191-194 on the same day. The stop's own notes cite woodcut 66 at folio 166 and woodcuts 67-70 at folio 167, which are the catalogued pages now known to be wrong.

Chapter XV is in fact pp.177-180, the nymph's discourse on the multitude of lovers. Chapter XVI is pp.181-188: the close of that triumph, a second garden of streams and dryads, and Poliphilo's long interior torment.

Second and related: moving 'priapus' to XVII left chapter XVI with NO tour stop, priapus having been its only one. That is a real gap made visible rather than a regression — chapters[].tour_stops for XVI is now empty — and its reading pages inherit 'triumphs'. XVI's features are already enumerated in the ledger and all unbuilt, so there is something for a stop to speak about.

**Acceptance.** The Vertumnus and Pomona stop carries a chapter tag and a 'pages' range that match the header of the page its lede describes, using the mechanism already in build_reading.py; its notes' folio citations are restated in the form 'page_seq NNN = our p. NNN' against the corrected plate pages; and either chapter XVI gains a stop of its own or the ledger records, with a reason, that it is deliberately without one.

**Risk.** Do not retag by pattern. Read each stop against the page its lede describes and that page's own header first — the failure this whole family of tickets is about. Note that 'triumphs' is tagged XIV as well, at a different stop, so a range will be needed to keep the two apart rather than a tag alone.

**Resolution.** Closed 2026-09-20 for the retag; the chapter-XVI question spun out. Settled by reading translation/en/ page by page against each page's own header, not by pattern: p.188 is the last page headed Chapter XVI (Poliphilo's interior torment), p.189 the first headed XVII, p.191 has Vertumnus 'sitting in triumph upon a most ancient car', p.192 the four-cornered altar in the meadow, p.193 Summer, Autumn and Winter's tag (and Dallington's last continuous page), and p.194 opens with Winter's marble and then the Priapus simulacrum -- which is where the priapus stop, and our own translation, both begin. So the Vertumnus and Pomona stop is chapter XVII, pages [189, 193], using the mechanism debt-reading-station-is-chapter-grained built; the priapus stop narrows from [189, 195] to [194, 195], which puts the hand-off stop exactly on the first page of our own translation; and the chapter-XIV triumphs stop gains its own explicit range [158, 176] -- coverage.json's independently derived pages_1499 for XIV -- so the two stops sharing the station 'triumphs' are kept apart by range and not by tag alone, as the risk note asked. The two folio citations in its notes are restated against the measured plate pages: woodcut 66 at page_seq 181 = our p.191, signed 'm iiii'; woodcuts 67-70 not on one leaf at all but spread over page_seq 182/183/184 = our pp.192/193/194. reading.json rebuilt: pp.189-193 move from priapus to triumphs and nothing else moves. CHAPTER XVI still has no stop, and now chapter XV has none either (pp.177-180, the nymph's discourse on the multitude of lovers, which this stop was never about); both chapters' pages inherit 'triumphs', which is at least narratively continuous. Writing a stop for either, and recording the reason in the ledger, needed research/coverage.json and new interpretive copy, both outside this pass: debt-chapters-xv-and-xvi-have-no-tour-stop.

**✅ done** · bug · priority 4 · hp-researcher

**Evidence.** Found 2026-09-20 during the plate sweep for bug-woodcut-catalog-page-jitter. coverage_seed.chapter_pages() derives every chapter's range from the 'Chapter NNN' in the first line of each translation/en/page_NNN.md, so a wrong header moves a chapter boundary. Headers run ... 091 VIII, 092 IX, 093 VIII, 094 IX ..., which gives VIII [79,93] and IX [92,116] — the only overlapping pair in the whole book (checked programmatically; the only other anomalies are the blank leaves).

The scan settles it. hp1499_p084.jpg — page_seq 84 = our p.94 — carries the capitalised argument of chapter IX ('QVANTA INSIGNE MAIESTATE FVE QVELLA DELLA REGINA, ET LA CONDITIONE DELLA SVA RESIDENTIA') with its decorated initial beneath, and the line above it ends '...la Regina Eleuteryllida.' So chapter IX opens at our p.94, and pages 92 and 93 both belong to chapter VIII. page_092.md's header is the error.

Note that coverage_seed.MEASURED_SECTIONS puts QUEEN_PALACE at page_seq 82 ('Chapter IX opens on page_seq 82') on the same bad evidence; that boundary wants moving to 84 at the same time.

**Acceptance.** translation/en/page_092.md is headed 'Chapter VIII', coverage_seed's derived ranges give VIII [79,93] and IX [94,116] with no overlap, and MEASURED_SECTIONS' QUEEN_PALACE boundary is 84 with the scan quoted as its basis. check_sections() still passes.

**Risk.** Small but real: an overlapping range means a plate on our pp.92-93 is filed by whichever chapter the dict happens to iterate first. Nothing in the ledger turns on it today. translation/ was outside the 2026-09-20 ledger pass's scope.

**Resolution.** DONE. translation/en/page_092.md is headed 'Chapter VIII'. The derived ranges are now VIII [79,93] and IX [94,116] — the overlap is gone, and a programmatic pass over all 38 chapters finds no remaining overlapping pair.

Checked against the text rather than taking the header's word for it: our pp.92 and 93 both carry on chapter VIII — p.92 the triglyphs and the patterned pavement of the area round the third fountain, p.93 the colonnade and its two hundred columns — while p.94 carries chapter IX's own argument about the majesty of the Queen and the condition of her dwelling, which is the English of the capitalised argument the scan shows at page_seq 84.

MEASURED_SECTIONS' QUEEN_PALACE boundary moved 82 to 84 with that scan quoted as its basis and the superseded reading recorded in its note. check_sections() passes: QUEEN_PALACE is now page_seq [84,106] = our [94,116], which is chapter IX's range exactly, and the sections still tile page_seq 1-457 with no gap or overlap.

NOT FIXED, outside this pass's scope: translation/manifest.json also records p.92 as chapter IX, and build_reading.py takes each page's chapter from the manifest rather than from the file header, so reading.json still labels our p.92 'IX'. ### `bug-woodcut-catalog-ten-unresolved-plates` — Ten plates have been opened at their catalogued page and found absent; their true pages are still unknown

**✅ done** · bug · priority 4 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Split out 2026-09-20 on closing bug-woodcut-catalog-page-jitter, which opened every near-boundary plate's scan. For these ten the catalogued page WAS opened and carries something else, and the true page was not found, so each is left where the catalogue put it and stamped page_unresolved in research/coverage.json (PLATE_PAGE_UNRESOLVED in scripts/coverage_seed.py holds what each catalogued page actually carries).

#66 (Vertumnus and Pomona) and #67-70 (the four Seasons reliefs) are the important ones: they are catalogued at page_seq 166-167, which the scans show carry the two halves of the fourth Bacchic triumph, and our translation puts their subjects at pp.190-193 = page_seq 180-183. Scan p180 is unbroken text, and the corpus folder holds no scan of page_seq 181-184 at all — so the plates cannot be located without a scan this project does not have. They are currently filed in chapters XIV and XV while their text is chapter XVII.

#86 (ruins of the Polyandrion among trees) is catalogued at 233, which carries the obelisk and one medallion; scan p234 carries two further hieroglyph blocks and not this one.

#127 (box-tree clipped as three peacocks) at 313 and #129 (flower-bed, two birds on a vase) at 317: both pages carry other plates and not these.

#83 and #162 are probably not lost at all but duplicate rows — #83 repeats #82's placeholder description on a page that carries one woodcut, and #162 repeats #161's scene on a page that carries one woodcut.

**Acceptance.** Each of the ten either has its true page_seq in PLATE_PAGE_FIXES with the identifying line of Italian, or is recorded as a duplicate catalogue row with the row it duplicates named. For #66-70 that needs scans of page_seq 181-184, which are not in C:\Dev\hypnerotomachia polyphili\site\images\woodcuts_1499 — fetching them is part of the work (scripts/fetch_1499_plates.py). Nothing is written into hp.db, which is read-only.

**Risk.** Low and bounded: all ten already carry page_checked, so nobody can mistake them for pages that were never looked at. The live consequence is that #66-70 sit in chapters XIV and XV in the ledger while xvii-seasons-altar and xvii-vertumnus-pomona-triumph, which they illustrate, sit in XVII.

**Resolution.** DONE — all ten, including #66-70, which the ticket expected to be blocked.

THE SCANS WERE FETCHABLE, but not the way the ticket supposed. scripts/fetch_1499_plates.py does not fetch anything: it is a local copy-and-downsize from the corpus folder into images/woodcuts_1499/, and it cannot acquire a page the corpus does not already hold. It also lives in THIS repo, not the corpus one. What resolved these is a second facsimile already on disk and not previously used for plate work: the ia_scan folder under the corpus staging directory, 301 full-page images covering roughly page_seq 170-468, read-only and never written to. Its numbering was calibrated at two anchors and then confirmed at four more: OUR PAGE = n + 5, so page_seq = n - 5. n201 is our p.206, the Medusa-oculus cistern in the temple; n190 is the full-page Priapus, our p.195 = page_seq 185 = plate #71.

RESOLVED TO A TRUE PAGE, now in PLATE_PAGE_FIXES, each with its identifying line of Italian:
  #66  166 to 181. The Vertumnus and Pomona car drawn by four horned fauns, under 'Sedendo ouante sopra una ueterrima Veha, da quatro cornigeri Fauni tirata', with the tablet beginning INTEGERRIMAM CORPOR. VALITVDINEM printed beneath the cut — the very inscription the ledger's xvii-vertumnus-trophy-inscription already quotes. The leaf is signed 'm iiii' at the foot, which is m4r on MEASURED_QUIRES and so an independent check on the page.
  #67  167 to 182. Spring, FLORIDO VERI S., the one relief on that leaf.
  #68  167 to 183. Summer, FLAVAE MESSI S., the upper of two reliefs on that leaf.
  #69  167 to 183. Autumn, MVSTVLENTO AVTVMNO S., the lower relief on the same leaf.
  #70  167 to 184. Winter, HYEMI AEOLIAE S. Page_seq 183 gives Winter's DESCRIPTION in the tapering colophon at its foot but not its cut; the relief heads the next leaf, beside the text about the marble veined with black to express a hail-filled sky — our p.194, the same page as the Priapus altar.
  #127 313 to 312. The clipped box carrying peacocks on the four-handled amphora, beside 'Fora dilquale usciua uno perpollito buxo ... sopra ciascuna uno pauone, cum le code demisse'.
  #129 317 to 314. The knot-bed with an eagle and a pheasant beak to beak footed on a vase, the border lettered SVPERNAE ALITIS BENIGNITAS.

NOT LOST PLATES AT ALL, three of the ten:
  #83 duplicates #82. Page_seq 213 carries one cut, and #81, #82 and #83 all carry the SAME placeholder description string, 'Temple ceremony continuation'.
  #162 duplicates #161. Scan opened: page_seq 419 carries exactly one cut — the mitred priestess enthroned, Poliphilo standing, Polia kneeling, the flaming altar-vase — answering both rows, which describe the same scene. Signed 'D', as MEASURED_QUIRES has it.
  #86 answers to NO WOODCUT. Page_seq 233 carries exactly two cuts, the plain obelisk and the round IVSTITIA medallion, which are #87 and #88. The ruined temple overgrown with ground-ivy and thorns that #86 describes is the TEXT of page_seq 232, and that leaf was opened too: unbroken text under a knotwork initial, with no cut on it at all. This is the inverse of the rule this ledger exists for — the catalogue can list MORE than the book draws, because its rows were made by subject-matching the text.

MACHINERY: PLATE_PAGE_UNRESOLVED is now empty, kept along with the branch that reads it for the next plate that genuinely cannot be placed. Two new tables, PLATE_DUPLICATE_ROWS and PLATE_NO_WOODCUT, carry the three above and stamp duplicates_plate and no_woodcut onto the ledger record. Seven new plate-to-chapter pairs (#66-70 XVII, #127 and #129 XXI) went into PLATE_CHAPTER_EXPECTED so check_plates() asserts them on every seed. Zero plates now carry page_unresolved.

### `debt-chapters-xv-and-xvi-have-no-tour-stop` — chapters XV (pp.177-180) and XVI (pp.181-188) have no tour stop at all; their reading pages inherit 'triumphs'

**✅ done** · debt · priority 5 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Opened 2026-09-20 closing bug-tours-triumphs-xv-stop-is-chapter-xvii, which carries the first half of this in its own evidence. Moving 'priapus' to XVII left XVI empty; moving 'Vertumnus and Pomona' to XVII, where its lede has always been set, now leaves XV empty too. Neither is a regression -- both chapters were being covered by a stop that describes another chapter's pages -- but the gap is real and is now visible in coverage.json's chapters[].tour_stops. XV is the nymph's discourse on the multitude of lovers; XVI is the close of that triumph, a second garden of streams and dryads, and Poliphilo's long interior torment (our pp.186-188 are the blazon of the demi-goddess and the speech he rehearses and rejects). Both chapters' features are already enumerated in the ledger and all unbuilt, so there is something for a stop to speak about.

**Acceptance.** Either each of XV and XVI carries a stop in tours.json with a page range read off the English (not off the tour prose), or research/coverage.json records for each, with a reason, that it is deliberately without one -- and coverage_seed.py is re-run either way so chapters[].tour_stops reflects the file.

**Risk.** Needs new interpretive copy, which means the citation discipline of project rule 2 and a reading of the chapter first; and it needs coverage.json, which was outside the closing pass's scope.

**Resolution.** READ both chapters in full against translation/en/ (pp.177-180 for XV, pp.181-188 for XVI) and checked every builder name in src/scenes/world/*.js (read-only, no code touched) before deciding. XV (pp.177-180) is the Nymph's discourse on the multitude of lovers: four unvisited six-horse cars 'surrounded' by countless nymphs and their lovers bearing torches, shrines and spoil-spears; an Elysian flower-meadow with a long named flower-catalogue; a roll-call of mortal girls the gods loved in disguise (Callisto, Antiope, Erigone, Ceres and the serpent, and many more); the Nymph's key speech that no earth-born creature may enter 'without a torch kindled' either by love and labour or by the company of three holy matrons, and her promise to quench hers at the temple; the 'My Poliphilo' recognition moment; and choirs of the ancient poets' mistresses (Lycoris, Nemesis, Delia, Corinna, Cynthia, and Sappho's Phaon among them) singing before each of the four cars. XVI (pp.181-188) opens with half a page closing that same triumph, then the Nymph leads Poliphilo to a SECOND garden -- a ring-shaped meadow of crystal streams closed round by wooded hills where nymphs bathe and wade with tame swans, weave garlands, kiss and mock-slap in play under named mythological shade trees (the Heliades' poplars, Daphne's laurel, the mulberry of Pyramus and Thisbe) -- then seven pages resolve into Poliphilo's long interior torment: doubting whether this is illusion, whether the Nymph is Polia, a vow to endure any labour to win her, a catalogue of self-torment similes (Tityus, Milo, the labyrinth, Actaeon's hounds, the ichneumon and crocodile), and a second, cautionary catalogue of mortals punished for presuming on the gods (Syrinx, Echo, Ulysses's men, Orion, Aesculapius/Phaethusa). DECISION, for both: NO STOP ADDED, in each case with a distinct reason recorded in research/coverage.json's chapters[].research.note (hand-edited field, preserved by coverage_seed.py). XV: the only built geometry anywhere nearby is _buildTriumphs (triumphs.js) -- chapter XIV's four cars of Jupiter's loves, already carrying their OWN tour stop at the 'triumphs' station (pp.158-176) whose lede already accounts for the generic riding nymph-musicians. XV's specific content -- named mistresses, the flower catalogue, the torch-rule speech -- is a different, wholly unbuilt scene playing out around the same built cars; a stop would have repeated the exact 'prose describes what the geometry does not' failure this project closed twice today (bug-tours-prose-ahead-of-geometry, bug-tours-triumphs-xv-stop-is-chapter-xvii). XVI: seven of its eight pages describe a locale -- the ring-shaped second garden -- that exists nowhere in the built world (grep for a ring of streams, bathing nymphs, swans, or any of the named trees/myths finds nothing; no plan.json precinct answers to it); a stop here would be the plain case the acceptance criterion itself names: pointing the tour at empty ground. Neither chapter's tours.json entry was touched (git status confirms it, unlike coverage.json). Both chapters' features (12 for XV, 11 for XVI) remain enumerated and unbuilt in the ledger, ready for whenever either scene is built. Re-ran coverage_seed.py after the coverage.json edit and confirmed chapters[].tour_stops for XV and XVI are both still empty and the research notes survived the re-seed (a hand-edited field, preserved from the prior ledger by chapter id). COVERAGE.md re-rendered. No hpDiag/live verification applies -- data/ledger-only pass, tours.json unchanged.
