### `debt-reading-plate-captions-come-from-a-jittery-column` — reading.json's plate captions are bound by woodcuts.page_1499, which disagrees with the corrected woodcut_catalog on 44 of the 159 plate pages; no caption has been checked against its own scan

**✅ done** · debt · priority 5 · hp-researcher
 · opened 2026-09-20, closed 2026-09-20


**Evidence.** Opened 2026-09-20 closing bug-plate-images-bound-to-page-seq-plus-eight. The IMAGE in Read mode is bound by filename and is now right, and verified by opening the file. The CAPTION beside it is not bound the same way: build_reading.py's plate_titles() reads `select page_1499, title from woodcuts` and adds the offset. page_1499 is a second LLM-assisted column, sibling to woodcut_catalog.page_seq, which bug-woodcut-catalog-page-jitter measured as good only to about two pages. Measured during this pass: build the same caption map from woodcut_catalog with coverage_seed's measured PLATE_PAGE_FIXES applied, and the two sources disagree on 44 of the pages that carry a plate -- e.g. our p.176 is 'Bacchic Triumphal Chariot' by one and 'Festive Scene at Fountain' by the other. Neither was checked against the scan, so which is right is unknown, and the pass did not guess: it left the caption mechanism alone. Where both agree the caption is visibly right (p.14 The Dark Forest, p.38 The Elephant and Obelisk).

PROGRESS 2026-09-20, second pass. The MECHANISM is fixed and shipped; the plate-by-plate sweep is part done and this ticket stays open for the remainder. Three things were established by opening scans that the ticket as written did not assume.

(1) THE COUNT IS LARGER THAN 44. Comparing the two sources by CATALOGUE ROW rather than by caption string — i.e. asking which rows each puts on each leaf, after dropping the rows coverage_seed has already measured as junk — they disagree on 63 of the 162 pages that carry a plate, driven by 22 catalogue rows that the two place on different pages. By caption string alone it is 67. The ticket's 44 appears to have counted only head-to-head conflicts where both columns name something.

(2) BOTH COLUMNS ARE JITTERY, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS IN DIFFERENT PARTS OF THE BOOK, so 'route the caption through woodcut_catalog' would have traded one set of wrong captions for another. Through the Temple of Venus and the Polyandrion the corrected catalogue runs about two pages EARLY and the old woodcuts column is right — #79 the two virgins with swans and doves is on p.220 not p.218, #80 the altar is on p.222 not p.220, #107 the hieroglyphic sarcophagus is on p.262 not p.260. Through the garden and the Adonis fountain the catalogue is right and woodcuts is wrong — #124 the square flower-bed ornament is on p.319, #126 the nine-compartment bed on p.321, #149 the Adonis tomb-fountain on p.373, #150 the Venus statue on p.375. And in several places NEITHER is right: #102 the Greek-lettered sepulchral urn is on p.257, which the catalogue puts at 259 and woodcuts at 260; #104 and #105 are both on p.260; #139 and #140, the sparking vase and the fuming amphora, are on pp.340 and 341 respectively, which is the old column's pair SWAPPED and is neither of the catalogue's placements.

(3) woodcuts.title IS NOT SAFE EVEN KEYED BY CATALOGUE NUMBER. The link between the two tables is itself unreliable: #24's catalogue description is 'Frieze ornament with genii, dolphins, bull skull' and the scan shows exactly that, while its woodcuts.title reads 'Queen Eleuterylida's Palace'. Same for #47, #63, #64, #66, #67, #102, #104. The caption text therefore comes from woodcut_catalog.description throughout, never from woodcuts.title.

WHAT SHIPS NOW. build_reading.py's plate_captions() resolves in three tiers: a hand-checked table PLATE_CAPTION_CHECKED for the 30 pages whose scan was opened in this pass, each entry carrying the identifying line of Italian or the inscription that settles it (three of the 30 are entered as None — pp.48, 94 and 161 were opened and carry NO woodcut at all, only unbroken text, so they are explicitly uncaptioned); then, for pages not checked, woodcut_catalog.description, but ONLY where exactly one catalogue row resolves to the page AND woodcuts.page_1499 independently agrees that that same row is on that same page — 69 pages, two separately-derived columns corroborating each other, and the ticket's own spot checks p.14 and p.38 are in this tier; and otherwise NO CAPTION. Junk rows (PLATE_NO_WOODCUT, PLATE_DUPLICATE_ROWS, PLATE_PAGE_UNRESOLVED) are dropped before any of it. reading.json now carries 96 captions on 162 plates, and the other 66 plates are deliberately uncaptioned rather than captioned on a guess. Under the old mechanism nearly all 159 were captioned and an unknown fraction were wrong.

REMAINDER FOR A FUTURE PASS: the 33 pages that are still contested and therefore still uncaptioned. In page order: 33, 159, 163, 165, 166, 167, 169, 170, 172, 214, 231, 244, 246, 255, 261, 268, 305, 322, 324, 327, 328, 329, 331, 337, 344, 347, 349, 397, 399, 400, 401, 403, 425, 426, 431, 445, 457, 458. Each needs its scan opened and an entry added to PLATE_CAPTION_CHECKED in the same form as the 30 already there.

**Acceptance.** Every captioned page in reading.json takes its caption through the same corrected page as the image -- one source, woodcut_catalog with PLATE_PAGE_FIXES applied -- and the 44 disagreements are each settled by opening the scan and recorded plate by plate, in the form the other plate tickets use. A caption naming a cut that is not the one on the page is the defect being closed.

**Risk.** Interpretive: a confident caption on the wrong picture is worse than no caption, and this is reader-facing copy under project rule 2.

**Resolution.** DONE. The remainder is discharged: all 38 pages this ticket listed were opened on the scan, and so were the other 25 uncaptioned leaves it did not list, which the sibling frame ticket had measured as having no catalogue row. 63 contested leaves in all, plus nine more opened in the course of the sweep (pp.164, 168, 191-194, 270, 306, 402) = 72 scans, each entered in PLATE_CAPTION_CHECKED in scripts/build_reading.py with the identifying line of Italian, the running head, the inscription or the gathering signature that settles it. The table now holds 102 leaves, 18 of them entered as None because the leaf was opened and carries no cut.

RESULT IN reading.json: 149 plates, 149 captions, NONE uncaptioned and none guessed. It was 162 plates and 96 captions at the start of the day, and 144 plates / 96 captions when this ticket's first pass stopped.

WHAT THE SWEEP SETTLED ABOUT THE CATALOGUE, all of it measured page by page. (1) THE WHOLE TRIUMPHS RUN IS ONE TO TWO LEAVES EARLY. Reading our pp.159-177 in order — car, then the two tabella panels, then the PARS ANTERIOR ET POSTERIOR panel, then the next car, with the running heads TRIVMPHVS | PRIMVS, TRIVMPHVS | SECVNDVS, TRIVMPHVS | TERTIVS reading across each opening — places #49-#57 and #61 each one or two pages on from where the catalogue files them. (2) THE TEMPLE AND THE POLYANDRION RUN EARLY TOO: #79, #80, #84, #85, #100, #108, #110, #111, #112 all move, and the Polyandrion's full-page monuments (Artemisia p.267, the Sertullius busts p.269, the Trebia portal p.271) were each one leaf off.
